Norway mourns King Harald as Haakon VIII ascends throne
- Published
Norwegians, politicians and royals are grieving the death of beloved King Harald V, as a period of national mourning begins and his son King Haakon VIII assumes the throne.
After Harald's death was announced early on Friday, crowds amassed at the royal palace in Oslo, laying flowers and flags, some mourners visibly in tears.
Hours later, the new king met government ministers for an extraordinary council of state meeting, after which the 53-year-old announced he was taking on the royal family's motto "All for Norway".
Harald died peacefully in hospital at 06:35 local time (04:35 GMT) aged 89, after receiving treatment there for a rare blood condition since last week.
The late monarch has been described as an inclusive, transparent and empathetic "people's king" who modernised the Norwegian monarchy.
European royals, including King Charles III - whose mother Queen Elizabeth II was Harald's second cousin - as well as political leaders and ordinary citizens, paid tribute to his service and the stability he brought to the country.
Norway's Prime Minister Jonas Gahr StÃ¸re, who laid flowers outside the palace and signed a book of condolences after greeting the new king, said the country was "united in grief and gratitude".
In a televised memorial address - one of multiple eulogies by ministers - he said the late king's "legacy lives on" and offered condolences to the royal family and Queen Sonja, who would have celebrated her 58th wedding anniversary with Harald on Saturday.
Norwegian national footballer Erling Haaland thanked Harald for "everything you meant to Norway" in a post on Instagram, adding that it had been an honour to meet him earlier in the summer at the palace following the Fifa World Cup.
In the country's capital, Norwegians shared their grief and affection for the late king.
"I personally will say he was everything for us, especially being an immigrant," Biteya Terfassa, an Oslo resident who was born in Ethiopia, told news agency Reuters outside the palace.
"He made us feel at home and he made us feel loved. So he was like a grandfather that I never had."
At noon, the Norwegian Armed Forces honoured Harald with a funeral salute of 21 shots from Akershus Fortress in central Oslo.
Later on Friday, a procession left the chapel at Rikshospitalet, where Harald died, and headed to the palace.

corpus.signal_text:
Norway's King Harald died Friday at 89, the Royal House of Norway announced.
"It is with deep grief that we announce that His Majesty King Harald has passed away," the royal palace said in a statement.
"King Harald died peacefully at Oslo University Hospital Rikshospitalet Friday 28 August at 6:35 AM," the statement continued.
NORWAY RAISES SECURITY CONCERNS OVER MANHATTAN-SIZED ARCTIC LAND SALE AS TENSIONS RISE
Harald, who was Europe's oldest living monarch, was hospitalized with a blood infection on Aug. 17.
He had previously received a pacemaker after falling ill during a vacation in Malaysia in 2024.
Harald announced he would be drawing down his number of public appearances that same year.
The monarch had served as Norway's head of state since 1991. He was Norway's first royal heir to be born in the country in more than 500 years. In 1905, after Norway gained its independence from Sweden, Harald's grandfather, King Haakon VII, became the first king of an independent Norwegian state since 1387.
Harald was viewed as a reformer and advocated for his fellow European royals to continue a trend towards openness with the public.
"If you've opened the gate it's very difficult to close it again," he told Reuters. "I'm not sure I'd want to close it. So far so good, as far as I'm concerned."
When the Nazis invaded Norway in 1940, Harald's mother fled with him, first to neutral Sweden, then to the United States, where they briefly lived in the White House after then-President Franklin Delano Roosevelt offered the pair safe haven.
Harald, his mother and his sisters soon moved to Bethesda, Maryland and would often meet with Roosevelt, who Harald said was like a grandfather to him.
Harald's son, Crown Prince Haakon, 53, will succeed him and take the name King Haakon VIII.
Haakon and his wife, who will become Queen Mette-Marit, have been embroiled in scandal since it was revealed she exchanged emails with and had multiple meetings with convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
CROWN PRINCESS METTE-MARIT OF NORWAY SAYS SHE REGRETS HER TIES TO JEFFREY EPSTEIN
Mette-Marit said she regrets her ties to the deceased billionaire and claimed she had no knowledge of his sordid past while communicating with him.
Additionally, Mette-Marit's son, Marius Borg Høiby, who she had from a previous marriage, was convicted of several charges of rape and domestic violence in June. He was sentenced to four years in prison, and both he and prosecutors are appealing the sentence.

corpus.title: Norwegians mourn King Harald as son succeeds to throne
corpus.signal_text:
Laying flowers and embracing, thousands of people gathered in Oslo on Friday to pay their respects to Norway’s King Harald, who died on Friday aged 89 after a reign of three and a half decades.
Harald’s 53-year-old son immediately succeeded him on the throne, announcing he would reign under the name King Haakon VIII.
Haakon takes over a monarchy long hailed for its modernity and modesty, but beset by a string of scandals in recent years.
A motor procession with King Harald’s casket left Oslo University Hospital on Friday evening, taking the late monarch on the 20-minute ride to the royal palace, televised images showed.
Members of the public braved the rainy weather to line the streets to catch a glimpse of the procession, which included the royal family.
King Haakon VIII had arrived at the palace just before lunch with his 22-year-old daughter Ingrid Alexandra — the new crown princess — to formally inform the government of his father’s death.
In a statement, Haakon thanked “the government and Norwegian people for their support and sympathy for the Royal Family at this time”.
“An era has ended. A new one begins. The king is dead. Long live the king,” Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store said in a speech shortly after meeting the new monarch.
“We will remember King Harald for his love for his people, for his humour and warmth, and for his unwavering faith in us,” he said.
Store was later seen laying down flowers in front of the palace.
Norway’s parliament said the new monarch would take an oath of allegiance in its main chamber on September 1.
The government announced a period of national mourning until Harald’s funeral, the date of which is yet to be set.
A king of his time
Europe’s oldest reigning monarch, King Harald, had been in hospital in Oslo since August 17, suffering from haemolytic anaemia, a condition caused by an abnormally rapid destruction of red blood cells that leads to fatigue and shortness of breath.
Store said Harald, who ascended to the throne in 1991, was “a king of his time and for his time”, noting that he accompanied Norway through decades of enormous change during which the country “grew richer, we became more numerous, and we became more diverse”.
Thousands of Norwegians massed outside the palace in Oslo as it began to rain. They laid down mountains of flowers, cards and red, white and blue national flags, and many hugged and held each other.
“He was the king of the people,” mourner Kristoffer Hamre told AFP.

Nach dem Tod von König Harald steht ein Thronwechsel in Norwegen an: Sein Sohn Haakon wird König. Seine Ehefrau Mette-Marit ist jetzt zur Königin ernannt worden.

corpus.title: Ex-President Niinistö: Norway's late King Harald was a 'wise elder'
corpus.signal_text:
Finnish politicians are reacting to the passing of the Norwegian king, Harald V, who died on Friday.
His successor, Crown Prince Haakon, immediately ascended the throne.
Norway's government on Friday declared a period of national mourning, which will continue until the king's funeral.
President Alexander Stubb expressed his condolences on the death of Harald in a post on X.
European Parliament member Anna-Maja Henriksson meanwhile said she shares the grief of the Norwegian people and the royal family.
President Niinistö pays warm tribute
Former Finnish President Sauli Niinistö described the late King Harald of Norway as a wise leader.
"He was not only a king but also a very good-humoured person," Niinistö told Yle in an interview.
Niinistö said the king was a "wise elder" who knew how to make his views count.
"He was very easy to talk to about a wide range of subjects, and he also used a lot of humour."
Harald had a very positive view of Finland, and Nordic cooperation was important to him. Their conversations sometimes touched on historical events as well.
Niinistö and King Harald met around ten times over the years at international gatherings.
"King Harald lived for his nation and its success. And now that nation carries on," Niinistö said.

corpus.title: Norwegens neuer König: Wer ist Haakon?
corpus.signal_text:
Norwegens neuer König: Wer ist Haakon?

Nach dem Tod seines Vaters Harald ist Haakon der neue König von Norwegen. Wer ist der neue Monarch? Und wie stehen die Norweger zu ihm?
